key_insight: SecureGARD governs tool-using LLM agents with explicit action semantics and task state, blocking unsafe execution while allowing bounded replanning for unmet obligations.
engineering_relevance: A shared semantic layer can enforce authorization across heterogeneous tools without indiscriminately blocking legitimate tasks.
method: Map tool calls into a shared semantic representation governed by an executable ontology.
Combine ontology rules with episode-level task state to classify actions as ready, waiting, or forbidden.
Refine ontology axioms offline using verified training executions, consistency checks, protected entailments, and held-out validation, then freeze the ontology.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 0% attack success rate on AgentDojo, ASB, and AgentDyn, with improved task utility under attack compared with existing baselines.
watch_item: Deployment depends on accurate tool semantics and state tracking; the reported benchmark results do not establish robustness to unseen tools or attacks.
paper_title: SecureGARD: Dynamic Ontology-Guided Governance for Secure Tool-Using LLM Agents
